title: Grade 3 Social Studies — Choices, Resources, and Trade
subject: Social Studies
description: Practice with questions on scarcity, opportunity cost, needs, wants.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: Which is usually a need rather than a want?
Which is usually a want rather than a basic need?
You have enough for a book or a soccer ball and choose the book. What did you give up?
choices: all other books in the store
the money in someone else's bag

questions.question: A class has six brushes for eight painters. Why must students make choices?
Which resource comes from nature?
choices: a wooden desk after it is made

questions.question: What is barter?
choices: using a card to pay cash price
trading goods or services without money

questions.question: Which is an example of a producer?
choices: a baker who makes rolls for sale
a bank customer waiting in line
a shopper who eats a roll

questions.question: How can a village benefit from trade with a nearby town?
choices: It must make all items itself.
It can get products it does not make.
It always stops selling its own products.

questions.question: What usually happens to time you spend on one activity?
choices: You can always repeat the hour.
You cannot use that same time for a different activity.

questions.question: Which action is saving?
choices: putting part of your money aside for a later purchase
buying the first thing you see
giving the price of a toy to a store

questions.question: Which is an example of a capital resource used to make goods?
Which choice shows specialization?
choices: One worker makes shoes and another repairs bikes.
Customers trade every job each hour.
Every worker makes every item alone.
One buyer changes the price signs.

questions.question: What is a budget?
If you need one notebook, which same-size one costs least?
A class chooses more books instead of more art paper. What is the class's opportunity cost?
choices: the extra art paper it gave up
the amount of time in a day

questions.question: Why might a farmer sell apples to people in a city?
choices: Every city already has free apples.
People in cities never buy food.
Selling apples makes them disappear from farms.
The farmer has apples and the buyers want them.

questions.question: When a choice is made because money is limited, what economic idea appears?
Which action compares tradeoffs?
choices: assuming the first backpack is always best
buying by color without checking anything else
refusing to look at any prices
checking both price and how long two backpacks might last

questions.question: Two stores sell equal bags of rice at different prices. What can help a buyer spend less?
choices: buy both bags because prices differ
compare prices for those same-size bags

questions.question: Which example uses money as a way to trade?
choices: paying a shop for a loaf of bread
trading a hat for a scarf without money
making a pencil as a gift
